title: 36 countries climbed into high income. Only one from East & Southeast Asia

voiceover.text: Since nineteen eighty-eight, thirty-six countries have climbed into the World Bank's high-income group.
From East and Southeast Asia? Just one.
The line today is about fourteen thousand dollars of income per person. And countries didn't cross it one by one. They came in waves.
First, Central and Eastern Europe. Seven countries in four years.
Then the commodity boom. Chile, Uruguay, Russia, Argentina, Venezuela.
But not all of them stayed. By twenty fifteen, Russia, Venezuela and Argentina had all fallen back.
Argentina made it twice, in twenty fourteen and twenty seventeen. Both times, it slipped back the very next year.
The fastest climb of all? Guyana. Oil started flowing, and income per person jumped from about six thousand dollars to over twenty-eight thousand, in six years.
Still, thirty-two of the thirty-six are high income today. So what does a climb that sticks look like?
South Korea made it in ninety-five. The Asian crisis knocked it back. Three years later it returned, and it has stayed ever since.
In twenty eleven, Thailand and China were neck and neck. Both well under half the line.
By twenty twenty-five, China was at ninety-nine percent.
Thailand passed the halfway mark in twenty eighteen. Seven years later, it's still just over half.
We found this on Querious, using the World Bank's official income history, year by year.
Find every move up, then download the result, or connect it to your own tools.
The data is open. The question is yours.
